paper.title_en: Higher-order lump and semi-rational solutions for the $(2+1)$-dimensional nonlocal Mel'nikov equation
paper.abstract_en: This paper systematically investigates the high-order lump solutions and semi-rational solutions of the $(2+1)$-dimensional nonlocal Mel'nikov equation satisfying the $\mathcal{PT}$-symmetric condition. By employing Hirota's bilinear method and the Kadomtsev-Petviashvili (KP) hierarchy reduction technique, the general determinant form of these solutions expressed in terms of Schur polynomials and exponential functions is established. Based on this framework, we classify first-order lump solutions into three types: bright lump, four-petaled lump, and dark lump, and further extend this classification to higher-order cases. The semi-rational solutions in which lumps coexist with dark solitons and breathers are constructed. Furthermore, we systematically analyze their dynamical behaviors, and elucidate the controlling role of parameter $a_k$ on the position of these lumps. This study not only extends the structure of the analytical solutions for the nonlocal Mel'nikov equation but also provides a theoretical foundation for understanding interaction mechanisms of nonlinear waves in the $\mathcal{PT}$-symmetric systems. These solutions have significant implications for fields such as optics, plasma physics, and fluid mechanics.
